messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected — large drop in exception event rate for project=prod-web. Event ingestion down to ~5% of baseline since 2025-03-12T10:42:00Z. Auto-suppression engaged. Link: https://sentry.internal/prod-web/alerts/5234

oncall-robert: I'm on it, looking at ingest logs and Sentry relay metrics

maria: seeing a spike of 429/401 from our auth provider when relay tries to fetch token. snippet from relay logs:
```
2025-03-12T10:41:38Z relay: POST /api/events -> 0 events accepted status=202
2025-03-12T10:41:39Z relay: auth_token_fetch failed status=429 retry_after=60
2025-03-12T10:41:39Z relay: dropping 120 events (rate_limited)
```

jake: confirmed from runtime side — our SDKs are getting 401/429 when requesting short-lived tokens from oauth-authz service. repeated 429s from x-auth-service. curl to introspect token endpoint returns 429 with error body "quota_exceeded"

eli: this looks like a third-party auth provider (idp) throttling incident. Could be a vendor-side global rate limiter. We should fail open for telemetry to avoid dropping events if possible, or switch to the backup service account key

oncall-robert: quick mitigation options:
- rotate to long-lived service key (prod-relay-service-key) that bypasses token endpoint
- increase client-side retries with exponential backoff
- enable local disk buffering in relay (drop to disk) to capture events for backfill

maria: tried rotating to service key — relay accepted events for ~30s then 429s resumed; looks like token endpoint not sole problem. Seeing 429s on the Sentry ingestion endpoint too, but headers show upstream auth-provider 429s in traces

jake: paging CS and Product for possible delayed triage; no user-visible errors reported yet, SSO login unaffected. Impact: missing exception telemetry -> delayed bug detection & delayed customer triage

tom: CS lead - please prepare proactive outreach for top 5 enterprise customers, note that error telemetry may be incomplete for the window 10:42-11:15 UTC. We'll prepare a short blurb.

pagerduty-bot: :pager: PagerDuty incident triggered (INC-1123). Escalation to Eng-SRE and Backend oncall.

eli: immediate action
1) enable disk buffering on relays (command below)
```
# enable buffering
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/relay RELAY_FAIL_ON_RATE_LIMIT=false RELAY_BUFFER_ENABLED=true
```
2) increase retry budget for token fetch
3) open support ticket with auth vendor, include debug logs and timestamps

maria: ran the k8s change, relays started persisting events locally. Event counts slowly climbing back to ~60% of baseline after 6m.

oncall-robert: good. I'll coordinate customer comms. Need a handoff to eli for next shift. Current status: partial mitigation (disk buffering + retries) in place; vendor ticket opened; still seeing intermittent 429s from auth provider. No production user impact reported beyond telemetry.

eli: taking over oncall. Runbook notes:
- keep buffering enabled until vendor confirms quota fixed
- run backfill script once vendor clears auth window: `scripts/backfill_sentry_events --since 2025-03-12T10:42:00Z`
- escalate to account manager if no vendor response in 30m

oncall-robert: handing off to eli. Summary for handoff: root cause suspected vendor-side auth throttling causing relay token fetch failures -> relay dropped events. Mitigations applied: service key rotation attempt, disk buffering enabled, retry policy tuned. Customer impact: missing/ delayed exception signals; CS notified and outgoing blurb drafted. Logs & traces attached to the vendor ticket.

eli: ack, I'll follow up and keep updates here. :thumbsup:

cs-lead: draft posted to customer channels and sent to top 5 customers. Will flag any incoming tickets. Keep me posted for postmortem.

incidents-bot: Incident thread marked as active. Next update requested in 30m or on notable state change.
